To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the point-form current is equivalent to the front-form current in the q^{+}=0 frame; 2) the front-form current is equivalent, in the limit of infinite invariant mass, to the usual front-form current obtained from a spectator current, and 3) the point-form approach is a suitable framework to investigate the electromagnetic form factors of spin-1 bound states.

(i) the Bakamjian–Thomas mass operator, which is the basic ingredient of our point-form approach, has the wrong cluster properties; (ii) these wrong cluster properties lead to spurious contributions in the electromagnetic bound-state current which are associated with the sum of the momenta of the constituents of the bound system; (iii) for a spin-0 bound system, like a charged pi meson, the spurious terms can be eliminated by solely choosing a large enough total invariant mass

(i) the Bakamjian–Thomas framework for bound-state systems with spin 1 is not suitable for the description of the electromagnetic properties, (ii) for spin-0 systems with a large invariant mass, the Bakamjian--Thomas approach is applicable, (iii) in both cases, the current can be expressed in terms of the bound-state wave function, which is a Lorentz scalar.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the electromagnetic form factors of few-body bound states in a point-form framework.
the electromagnetic properties of bound systems in the context of point-form quantum mechanics and the associated Bakamjian- Thomas mass operator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the elastic form factors, the point-form current is equivalent to the front-form current for all spin-0 systems and for all spin-1 systems if the invariant mass is sufficiently large.
the point-form current is equivalent with the front-form current, provided that a suitable frame is used.
our current is physical, but not manifestly Lorentz-invariant, whereas the current from the front-form approach is manifestly Lorentinvariant, but not physical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Bakamjian–Thomas framework, when used in the point-form approach, provides an elegant and consistent description of the elastic electron scattering by the two-body bound state and the electromagnetic properties of the bound state.

, for spin-0 systems like the pion, the point-form approach and the light-front approach are equivalent in the limit of infinite invariant mass of the system, while for spin-1 systems like the deuteron, the equivalence is only partial.
we have shown that the Poincare-invariance of our approach is sufficient for the correct description of electromagnetic properties of few-body systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Bakamjian--Thomas framework for relativistic bound states is not only a convenient starting point for a Poincare invariant approach to bound-state dynamics, but also a useful tool to investigate the structure of the bound-state current.

the Bakamjian--Thomas mass operator provides a useful tool for the investigation of the electromagnetic properties of few-body systems in the point-form approach, even though it has the disadvantage of being not fully covariant.
, even though the point-form approach is a non-covariant approach, it is possible to extract a covariant bound-state current.
